subject: CCPA/CPRA: service provider vs operator binding language (AcmePay & ResellCo)
messages:
From: Monica Thompson <monica.thompson@acmepay.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DPO, AcmePay <privacy@acmepay.com>, legal@resellco.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CCPA/CPRA language -- service provider vs operator

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our standard addendum and a short redline from our legal team (AcmePay_DPA_redline_v3.pdf). Two quick asks up front: 1) we need explicit operator language for any reseller/resale scenarios so AcmePay can rely on the downstream vendor commitments; and 2) we need an onshore fallback commitment for telemetry exports (US-only routing) for regulated merchants.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can accept operator-style contractual commitments in resale paths and whether you have an onshore fallback SLA we can reference?

Appreciate it — Monica

--
Monica Thompson
Head of Legal Operations, AcmePay
monica.thompson@acmepay.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Thompson <monica.thompson@acmepay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA language -- service provider vs operator

Monica — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Quick summary from our side:

- Resale/reseller paths: Redwood typically contracts as a service provider (CCPA "service provider") to the direct customer. For certified resellers we can add a specific reseller appendix that requires the reseller to be designated as a controller/operator for its own business purposes, and to adopt equivalent contractual commitments to AcmePay. That does NOT automatically convert Redwood into an operator for the original data controller (AcmePay).

- Contract language: we can accept a limited operator-style obligation scoped only to the specific resale flow (e.g., where Redwood acts on behalf of ResellCo in routing/transforming). We would need narrow bright-line conditions (routing, purpose, and explicit customer instruction).

- Onshore fallback / telemetry: we have an onshore fallback plan (US regions) for telemetry/aggregates; we can commit to routing telemetry-derived exports to US-hosted storage for accounts in regulated verticals subject to capacity-based exceptions and 30-day notice.

I'll loop in Marissa for DPA redline details and Aditya for telemetry/infrastructure SLA language. Attaching our operator_vs_service-provider-matrix.xlsx for internal clarity.

Next steps: Marissa will propose redline language; Aditya will confirm the routing SLA and an example clause for the onshore fallback. Can you share the reseller agreement or confirm whether ResellCo will be acting under AcmePay's contract or as a separate reseller?

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Thompson <monica.thompson@acmepay.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redline: operator-ish clause for resale path (for review)

Monica / Kimberly team — attaching a proposed redline to AcmePay_DPA_redline_v3.pdf. Key points in this draft:

- Section 3.2 (Reseller operations): "Where Redwood processes Personal Information solely at the instruction of ResellCo acting under an AcmePay-authorized reseller model, Redwood shall act as a Service Provider to AcmePay; notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall accept, limitedly and solely for the duration of the ResellCo instruction, the following operator-like restrictions: (i) explicit prohibition on any resale or secondary use beyond the reseller instruction; (ii) immediate suspension of cross-border telemetry sharing without affirmative AcmePay consent; and (iii) contractually enforceable audit rights for AcmePay over ResellCo subprocessor onboards."

- We added an onshore fallback clause that references a specific regional routing commitment and an exception if capacity or compliance prevents routing (Redwood to notify within 5 business days and provide mitigation).

We intentionally kept the operator-style commitments narrow to avoid a broad reclassification under CCPA/CPRA which would impose statutory obligations on Redwood. Please review and tell us if the language still looks insufficient for AcmePay's compliance team.

Attachments: redline (embedded as part of the Drive link).

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

From: DPO, AcmePay <privacy@acmepay.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Thompson <monica.thompson@acmepay.com>, legal@resellco.com
Date: 2026-09-01T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline: operator-ish clause for resale path (for review)

Marissa / Kimberly — thanks for the rapid turnaround. A few concerns from AcmePay legal:

1) The reseller append allows Redwood to remain a "service provider" in AcmePay's chain, but we need stronger contractual guarantees that ResellCo will not attempt to assert independent controller status for derived telemetry. Can the audit right be extended to allow AcmePay to request proof of processing instructions (log excerpt) within 10 business days?

2) Onshore fallback: the proposed exception window (notify within 5 business days) is OK, but we need a maximum remediation timeline (60 days) and the option for AcmePay to require a temporary onshore cache/compensating control while remediation proceeds.

3) Subprocessor list: please share your current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessor processes AcmePay-identifiable data outside the US. We need the CSV.

We appreciate the limited operator commitments, but AcmePay's procurement needs the above stronger operational controls documented.

— DPO

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: DPO, AcmePay <privacy@acmepay.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Thompson <monica.thompson@acmepay.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline: operator-ish clause for resale path (for review)

DPO / Monica / Marissa — quick update from infra and product: 

- Subprocessor list attached (subprocessor_list_aug2026.csv). We have three subprocessors that handle telemetry aggregation and analytics; two of those operate in multi-region modes including EU and US. None of the telemetry subprocessors store raw AcmePay PII outside the US for accounts marked as US-regulated if the customer sets the region to US. We can add a contractual obligation to keep AcmePay-marked accounts' telemetry in US regions unless AcmePay opts into cross-region exports.

- Audit/log excerpt: we can provide redacted proof of processing instructions (logs showing routing) within 10 business days; for full log access we'd propose a controlled audit with NDA & scoped redaction.

- Onshore fallback remediation: we can commit to a 45-day remediation window for routing fixes and support a temporary onshore cache for critical customers during remediation as a compensating control.

I will update the redline to reflect: 1) 10-business-day log excerpt commitment; 2) 45-day max remediation; 3) optional temporary onshore cache; and 4) explicit condition that Redwood will ensure subprocessors honor the US-region restriction for accounts designated as US-regulated.

If that aligns, Marissa will produce a final redline for signature and we can coordinate a short call with ResellCo (Matt) to confirm their reseller model.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Product Manager, Platform Services | Redwood Inference

--
